name: Legacy Data Loading
apex: A deprecated wizard-driven feature letting end users import data into an existing schema table via a generated 4-page Data Load Wizard; New Data Loading superseded it with XLSX/XML/JSON, design-time column mapping, and up to 300 columns versus 45.
workflow: Developer runs Create Page Wizard > Legacy Data Loading, sets the upload table and unique key columns, adds transformation rules and lookups, then generates four wizard pages.
relevance: Superseded by New Data Loading (already logged) inside APEX itself; Paddock authors content via files/DB, not end-user spreadsheet uploads, so no wizard of this shape is needed.
skip_for_web: Whole feature - no spreadsheet-upload-to-table workflow exists on a content site.

name: Re-creating Generated Pages Instead of Editing Them
apex: Oracle's recommended pattern for wizard-generated pages: when a Data Load Wizard's pages need to change, re-run the wizard against the existing Data Load Definition to regenerate fresh pages instead of hand-editing the output.
attributes: Data Load Definitions (Shared Components > Data References)
Create Pages using this Legacy Data load
workflow: Developer opens the existing Data Load Definition, clicks 'Create Pages using this Legacy Data load', re-supplies page attributes, and regenerates the pages.
relevance: Genuine transferable discipline: keep the design definition as the single source of truth and regenerate scaffolded pages from it rather than hand-editing output, which Paddock's weekly git export should also respect.

name: Legacy Tabular Form
apex: A deprecated page type editing many table rows at once from one page via built-in Multi Row Update/Delete DML with checksum-based optimistic locking; creating new ones is desupported in favor of Interactive Grid.
attributes: hidden or display-only primary key columns
workflow: Developer builds a SQL-query report with editable columns bound to a table; on submit, MRU/MRD processes bulk insert, update, or delete rows keyed by primary key and row number.
relevance: Oracle blocks creating new tabular forms, pointing developers to Interactive Grid instead (already studied); Paddock has no bulk-row-edit grid need and would model one on Interactive Grid, not this.
skip_for_web: Entire component - legacy, new creation disabled by Oracle itself.

name: Legacy Web Service Reference
apex: A stored definition of an external SOAP or REST call (URL, method, auth, envelope or parameters) built via wizard from a WSDL document, RESTful details, or manual entry; new ones are only supported for apps that already have them.
workflow: Developer runs the wizard from Shared Components > Legacy Web Service References, supplies WSDL URL or REST/manual details, then tests the call in a built-in request/response harness.
relevance: Fully superseded by REST Data Sources (already logged) and frozen by Oracle to pre-existing apps only; Paddock's outbound HTTP calls live in lib/*.ts fetch code, not a declarative reference repository.
skip_for_web: The whole reference-repository concept, and its SOAP/WSDL half entirely.

name: Create Form/Report on Web Service Wizard
apex: Wizards that auto-generate an input form, submit button, and/or report page wired directly to a saved Web Service Reference's operation, mapping its input and output parameters to page items and report columns.
attributes: Input Items (Create Yes/No, Item Name, Item Label)
workflow: Developer picks Legacy Pages > Report/Form on Legacy Web Service in Create Page, chooses the reference and operation, then maps parameters to page items.
relevance: A one-off code-generation wizard around a deprecated integration mechanism; Paddock's general-component designer composes pages from persisted component definitions, not per-call generated forms.

name: Web Service Page Process
apex: A page process of Type=Web Service that invokes a saved Web Service Reference's operation at a chosen processing point, storing results into items or a collection, with editable In Parameters and Out Parameters.
attributes: Store Result In: Item(s) or Collection
workflow: Developer adds a process in Page Designer, sets Type to Web Service, picks the operation, and maps its parameters like any other process.
relevance: Declarative external-call-as-process has no equivalent in Paddock, where outbound calls are plain async functions in lib/ code rather than a page-process type a designer exposes.
skip_for_web: The declarative process-type wrapper around the call.

name: Oracle APEX Component Limits
apex: A reference appendix of hard numeric ceilings per legacy component type - byte, row, and column limits - that developers design around when using data loading, forms, interactive reports, tabular forms, and validations.
attributes: Print-server export: 32k header sub-template, about 26 columns
Forms: 32767 bytes per text area/rich text item; 2 PK columns or a ROWID
Interactive reports: 999 rows per column-heading filter; chart max 10000 data points
Item names: max 30 characters for bind-variable reference
Native PDF: a row may span multiple lines with one page break, then truncates
Native Excel: cell text truncates past 32k
Tabular Forms: 1 per page; 50 editable columns (g_f01-g_f50)
Validations: max 3950 characters of validation text
relevance: Ceilings are Oracle-DB/PL-SQL specific (bind-variable byte limits, g_f01-g_f50 arrays) with no Cloudflare/Next.js analog; Paddock already tracks its own ceiling (Worker's 64MiB uncompressed) independently.
skip_for_web: Every specific number here; none maps onto this stack.

name: Export Directory Structure (Split into Multiple Files)
apex: The fixed folder taxonomy APEX writes to when an application, page, or component export is split into separate files (Split into Multiple Files / Export as Zip) - one subfolder per component type, several levels deep.
relevance: Direct precedent for Paddock's own git-branch design export: group exported components by kind into named subfolders (pages/, lists/, computations/, settings/) instead of one flat dump, exactly as APEX does.

name: Workspace-level vs Application-level Export Scope
apex: Within the same export taxonomy, a few component kinds - Credential, Workspace Static File, Remote Server - are written under a workspace/ root rather than application/, separating instance-wide objects from per-app ones.
relevance: Mirrors a split Paddock will need: site-wide design assets (the shared components library) versus per-page config should export into visibly distinct top-level folders, not be flattened together.

name: APEX Session to Database Session Correlation
apex: Because pooled connections mean no fixed APEX-session-to-DB-session mapping, APEX stamps each active DB session with client_id, client_info, module, and action strings so admins can identify which app, user, and step a session currently serves.
attributes: session longops: progress of long-running work
workflow: Developer or admin reads these columns from v$session, v$sqlarea, or v$session_longops during a live investigation, or sets them from custom PL/SQL via DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO.
relevance: The pattern - tag every request with a structured module/action identifier so ops can trace a live request through the system - fits Paddock's planned Debug panel and Health page for Worker/Supabase calls.
skip_for_web: The specific Oracle views (v$session) and DBMS_APPLICATION_INFO calls.

name: Per-subsystem Action Tagging Convention
apex: APEX assigns distinct action string formats per subsystem - SQL Workshop, Data Workshop, Automations, Installer - down to per-phase markers like automation-static-id:I (init), :R (row), :B (before action), :A (action N), :T (cleanup).
relevance: A concrete phase-naming scheme worth copying for Paddock's Debug panel: label each step of a multi-stage job (warm-live-data's fetch/parse/persist phases) with a short, greppable phase code.

name: Conditions
apex: The full catalog of declarative condition types selectable on any region, item, button, tab, list, navigation bar, process, computation, or validation, controlling whether it renders or executes without custom code.
attributes: Request is NOT contained in Value
Item is NOT NULL and NOT zero
Item is in colon delimited list
Item is NOT in colon delimited list
Current Page is in comma delimited list
Current Page is NOT in comma delimited list
Current page is in Printer Friendly mode
Current page is NOT in Printer Friendly mode
User is the public user (user has not authenticated)
Current Language is contained in Value
Current Language is NOT contained in Value
workflow: Developer picks a Condition Type on the component's Server-side Condition attribute, optionally supplies a Value, Page, or Expression, and APEX evaluates it before render or execution.
relevance: Core to 'components first': Paddock Developer's general components need this exact kind of declarative, reusable show/hide vocabulary (item/page/auth/request comparisons plus a hard 'Never') instead of bespoke per-component flags.

name: Recommended Direct Grants to Database Users
apex: A recommended list of schema-level GRANT statements APEX suggests issuing to a workspace's schema owner so the workspace can create typical objects, since APEX itself grants nothing beyond baseline access when a workspace is provisioned on an existing schema.
relevance: Oracle schema-privilege GRANT syntax has no analog in Supabase, which uses Postgres roles and RLS policies instead of per-workspace schema grants; nothing here informs Paddock's designer.
skip_for_web: The entire GRANT list - wrong database and wrong permission model.

name: Privileges Granted to PUBLIC (reserved APEX namespace)
apex: The set of packages, procedures, functions, tables, views, sequences, and types owned by the APEX product schema that carry PUBLIC synonyms and PUBLIC execute or select grants; Oracle warns against naming your own database objects the same.
relevance: A reserved-namespace collision list specific to Oracle's product schema; Paddock's naming-collision surface is Supabase table and column names, an unrelated namespace with no equivalent registry to consult.
skip_for_web: The entire symbol list - irrelevant namespace for this stack.
